book_title: Chapter 3: Follow the Dollar — GTM Funnel, Regulatory Audits & ₹100 Unit Economics
question: How does Sai Life Sciences win and retain global pharma contracts, what happens inside its supply chain and working capital cycle, and where does every ₹100 of FY26 revenue actually go?

epigraph.quote: The performance was broad-based, with both CRO and CDMO delivering healthy growth, while EBITDA margins stood steady around 27%–28%.
epigraph.author: Sivaramakrishnan Chittor, Whole-Time Director & CFO, Sai Life Sciences

web_blocks.title: Direct Business Development & The Integrated GTM Funnel

web_blocks.html: Sai Life does not use distributors or generic brokers. It sells through a direct, scientist-led business development (BD) team placed inside global biotech hubs—Watertown (Greater Boston), Manchester (Alderley Park), Europe, and Japan [17, 19]. Innovator pharma firms rarely switch plants once a drug enters Phase II/III trials or NDA filings. Winning the client early is everything. Sai Life runs a 'land-and-expand' funnel. A biotech or large pharma team starts with a small Fee-for-Service (FFS) synthesis or route study, moves up to a multi-year FTE discovery team, and later locks in commercial API supply at Bidar [14, 20].

This sticky funnel shows up in client tenure. Sai Life serves 18 of the top 25 global pharma companies, with tenures over 10 to 12 years across core accounts [18]. In Q1 and Q2 FY27, several major pharma clients upgraded from single projects to full integrated deals [9, 10]. Still, client concentration is a key watchpoint. The largest client brings in ~12% of revenue, the top 5 bring 37%, and the top 10 bring 54% [18].

web_blocks.title: Regulatory Qualification, Supply Chain & Working Capital Mechanics

web_blocks.html: In regulated CDMO work, clean audit clearance is the license to operate. Unit II (Hyderabad R&D) and Unit IV (Bidar API) have cleared multiple USFDA GMP audits and Pre-Approval Inspections (PAIs) with EIRs, plus PMDA and European audits [4, 23]. Any lapse in data integrity, containment controls, or OOS probes can trigger an FDA Form 483 or Warning Letter and halt shipments fast [23].

On the supply side, Sai Life buys specialty starting materials, clean solvents, chiral catalysts, and key intermediates. These cost ₹571 Cr (26.05% of sales) in FY26, up from ₹466 Cr (27.49%) in FY25 [15, 16]. Multi-step NCE synthesis ties up cash in work-in-progress (WIP) and safety stock. Inventory Days stood at 97 days in FY26 (up from 72 in FY24), while Debtor Days fell from 102 in FY22 to 62 in FY26 [1]. With 182 Days Payable, the Cash Conversion Cycle was -24 days in FY26. Broader Working Capital Days rose from 12 in FY24 to 70 in FY26 as commercial scale and capex grew [1].

The waterfall below breaks down every ₹100 of audited FY26 sales (₹2,192 Cr) into profit, operating cash flow (₹509 Cr), and free cash flow (-₹83 Cr per Screener) [1, 16]. Notice the cost mix of a science-led CRDMO: staff costs (₹31.16 per ₹100) exceed raw materials (₹26.05 per ₹100) [16]. That high people-cost base drives strong operating leverage when labs and plants fill up. That is how EBITDA margin jumped from 24.2% in FY25 to 28.9% in FY26 [1].

book_paragraphs: If you want to know how sticky a CRDMO's revenue really is, ignore the marketing brochures and look at how the sales force works. Sai Life Sciences has no distributors, no wholesalers, and no retail channels. Its business development teams sit directly in Watertown near Boston, in Manchester's Alderley Park, across European pharma corridors, and in Japan. Their job is to get a foot in the door early—maybe with a modest fee-for-service synthesis contract or a route-scouting study—and then turn that into a multi-year Full-Time Equivalent research team.

Why does that matter? Because once a Western pharma company registers a synthetic route and an analytical control strategy with the USFDA or Japan's PMDA, switching suppliers mid-stream is a regulatory nightmare. That switching friction explains why Sai Life works with 18 of the top 25 global pharma companies and boasts average tenures above ten to twelve years with its core accounts. Yet you and I must also respect the flip side of that intimacy: customer concentration. The top 10 clients still bring in 54% of revenue, the top 5 bring 37%, and the single largest client brings 12%. Lose one blockbuster program to a clinical failure or an internal reshoring decision, and you feel it immediately.

Now let's walk through every ₹100 of FY26 revenue together so you can see the unit economics with zero hand-waving. Out of ₹2,192 crore in FY26 sales, raw materials and chemical intermediates consumed just ₹26.05 per ₹100. The bigger bill—₹31.16 per ₹100—went to people: PhD chemists, biologists, process engineers, and global site leads. Add ₹13.91 for power, solvents, and facility overhead, and Sai Life kept ₹28.88 per ₹100 as operating EBITDA.

Because the December 2024 IPO wiped out most of the legacy debt, interest consumed only ₹1.87 per ₹100 in FY26, down from more than ₹6 per ₹100 two years earlier. After ₹7.62 for depreciation and ₹5.34 for taxes, ₹15.92 per ₹100 landed as net profit. Better still, ₹23.22 per ₹100 converted into actual operating cash flow—₹509 crore in total. Why, then, was free cash flow negative at -₹83 crore? Because management plowed ₹592 crore (₹27.01 per ₹100, or ₹633 crore on a gross capex basis) straight back into new reactors and labs. In short, Sai Life's existing factories are cash machines, but the company is currently reinvesting more than 100% of its operating cash flow to build tomorrow's capacity.

book_subsections.title: The Working Capital & Regulatory Tightrope
paragraphs: Every CDMO lives on a tightrope between inventory readiness and working capital bloat. In FY26, Sai Life carried 97 days of inventory—reasonable for multi-step custom synthesis, though up from 72 days in FY24—while collecting from customers in a crisp 62 days. Broad working capital days rose from 12 days in FY24 to 70 days in FY26 as commercial scale expanded.

Above all, never forget the regulatory pass/fail switch: Bidar and Hyderabad have cleared USFDA and PMDA inspections, but in export-only innovator manufacturing, a single serious Form 483 or data-integrity observation can freeze shipments far faster than any demand slowdown.

book_subsections.title: Why FTE and Commercial Supply Complement Each Other
paragraphs: Think of the two contract models as ballast and propulsion. Dedicated FTE contracts in discovery chemistry and biology give Sai Life high-visibility, recurring quarterly billing with minimal working capital tie-up, covering the fixed cost of scientific talent. Commercial CDMO batches in Bidar carry higher inventory and reactor intensity, but deliver superior operating leverage once volumes scale.

book_subsections.title: Fixed-Cost Leverage and the Anatomy of a 29% Margin
paragraphs: Look again at the cost structure we uncovered in the ₹100 unit-economics breakdown: ₹31.16 per ₹100 goes to scientific and engineering payroll, ₹26.05 goes to chemical raw materials, and ₹13.91 goes to facility overhead. Notice what that implies when revenue accelerates from ₹1,465 crore in FY24 to ₹2,192 crore in FY26. Raw materials scale roughly linearly with batch volume, but senior PhD leadership, quality assurance teams, and Manchester/Boston infrastructure scale far more slowly.

That operational gearing is a double-edged sword that every CRDMO student must respect. On the way up, incremental commercial batches at Bidar drop forty to fifty paise of every marginal rupee straight to EBITDA, lifting operating margins from 14% to 29%. On the way down—if a major commercial molecule faces inventory destocking or a Phase III trial fails—those same fixed scientific payroll and depreciation charges compress margins just as rapidly.

book_subsections.title: Working Capital Discipline in Multi-Step Custom Synthesis
paragraphs: Why did Working Capital Days rise from 12 days in FY24 to 70 days in FY26? In custom synthesis, complex molecules often require eight to fifteen sequential chemical steps, specialty catalysts, and imported chiral building blocks. As commercial batch sizes scale up at Bidar, work-in-progress inventory naturally sits on the balance sheet longer before final release testing and customer shipment.

Separating healthy growth-driven inventory from slow-moving or disputed receivables is crucial. Because Sai Life's debtor days actually improved to 62 days in FY26 while inventory rose to 97 days, the working-capital expansion reflects commercial scale-up rather than distressed collections—though keeping that total cycle below 80 to 85 days remains essential.

book_subsections.title: Why Direct Scientific BD Outperforms Distributor Models
paragraphs: Think about how rare Sai Life's customer-acquisition economics are compared to industrial or consumer businesses. Because there are no middlemen, dealers, or regional distributors taking a 10% to 15% cut, every rupee of contract value flows directly to Sai Life's top line. Instead of trade promotions, the company invests in PhD business-development scientists stationed in Boston, Manchester, Europe, and Tokyo who speak the exact technical language of client medicinal chemists.

That direct model creates a slow initial sales cycle—winning a master services agreement with a top-25 pharmaceutical company can take twelve to eighteen months of quality audits—but once established, those relationships last a decade or longer and require almost zero incremental marketing spend to renew.

book_subsections.title: Understanding the Capex-to-CFO Lag in Custom Manufacturing
paragraphs: Never confuse a negative free-cash-flow year in a growing CDMO with poor unit economics. In FY26, Sai Life's existing plants generated ₹509 crore of real operating cash flow—more than ₹23 out of every ₹100 of sales. The only reason free cash flow printed -₹83 crore is that management reinvested ₹592 crore into new reactors that will generate cash in FY28 and beyond.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
book_callouts.text: Look at that payroll-to-materials ratio: ₹31.16 for people versus ₹26.05 for raw materials per ₹100 of sales. That tells you Sai Life is selling intellectual chemistry and regulatory reliability, not commodity chemical tonnage—which is exactly why utilization swings drive such dramatic margin expansion and contraction.
